    Architecture

    Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery

    Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.

    hard · ~30m

  • 02
    Architecture

    Handling Asymmetric Network Partitions & Split-Brain

    A 3-node Raft metadata control plane (Nodes A, B, C across us-east-1a/1b/1c, 4,500 lock ops/sec, 100 ms heartbeat, 500 ms election timeout) suffers an asymmetric BGP/ACL drop between A and C while A<->B and B<->C stay healthy at 0.8 ms RTT. Prevent term-inflation livelock, zombie leader stale reads, and delayed split-brain writes.

    hard · ~30m
    ↗
  • 03
    Engineering

    Non-Blocking Async & Structured Logging

    A 20-pod Spring Boot order service (200 Tomcat worker threads/pod, 1,800 RPS/pod, 6 log lines/req = 10,800 events/sec or ~8.1 MB/s) stalls on `FileOutputStream.writeBytes` when shared gp3 EBS (3,000 IOPS) saturates. Decouple HTTP worker threads from disk I/O within a 64 MB log buffer budget while preserving ERROR/FATAL logs.

    medium · ~30m
    ↗
  • 04
    Engineering

    Automating TLS Certificate Rotation & Expiry Alerts

    A 90-day TLS certificate on `api.globalshop.com` expired at the CDN edge across 120 PoPs, failing 100% of user traffic with `ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID` while internal origin health checks stayed `200 OK` and an ACME DNS-01 cron failed silently 21 days earlier. Design a zero-touch TLS lifecycle and edge-aware observability architecture for 45 wildcard/SAN domains.

    medium · ~30m
    ↗
  • 05
    Architecture

    Avoiding Partition Hotspots on Monotonic Keys

    An IoT platform ingests 250,000 events/sec (~500 B each = 125 MB/s, 450 GB/hr) into a 16-node ScyllaDB/Cassandra cluster (RF=3) keyed by `(event_hour, created_at, device_id)`. One hot node hits 98% CPU and 1,400 ms p99 write latency while 15 nodes sit at 6% CPU. Redesign the partition key and query path to keep partitions < 100 MB and p99 write < 15 ms.

    medium · ~30m
    ↗
  • 06
    Architecture

    Why Implicit Type Coercion Breaks B-Tree Indexes

    On a 50M-row `users` table (`22 GB`, `3,500 QPS`, `phone_number VARCHAR(20)` with B-Tree `idx_users_phone`), `SELECT id, password_hash FROM users WHERE phone_number = ?` jumps from 2 ms to 18 seconds, pegging CPU at 100% and 40,000 read IOPS after a DTO changed `phoneNumber` from `String` to `Long`. Deploy a zero-downtime fix.

  • 07
    Engineering

    Zero-Downtime Blue-Green Database Deployments

    A 2,000 RPS payments service shares one PostgreSQL 15 database across Blue (v41) and Green (v42) behind an AWS ALB (60 s drain). Green's Flyway migration renamed `billing_zip` to `postal_code` and added `tax_jurisdiction NOT NULL` without a default, breaking Blue rollback with 100% HTTP 500s. Design an instant-rollback (< 30 s) Blue-Green schema pipeline.

    hard · ~30m

    Low-Level Design

    Bounding Task Queues to Prevent Heap OOM

    An ingestion service (15,000 events/sec, 8 KB payloads, `-Xmx2048m`) dispatches tasks into `Executors.newFixedThreadPool(16)` to write to Elasticsearch. During a 45-second ES GC pause (200 writes/sec), the hidden unbounded `LinkedBlockingQueue` buffers 675,000+ closures (5.4 GB) and crashes with `OutOfMemoryError`. Bound memory <= 64 MB and propagate backpressure.

  • 09
    Architecture

    Bulkhead Pattern: Isolating Faults & Capacity

    A checkout BFF (20 pods, 60 req/s/pod = 1,200 req/s, 200 Tomcat threads, one shared `PoolingHttpClientConnectionManager(maxTotal=200)`) fans out to `InventoryService` (p99=25 ms, SLA 150 ms), `PricingService` (p99=40 ms, SLA 200 ms), and non-critical `RecommendationService` (p99=80 ms). When `RecommendationService` stalls to 10 s, all 200 connections saturate in 3.3 s, causing a 100% checkout outage. Isolate capacity.

    Low-Level Design

    Bypassing Python GIL Contention in CPU Pipelines

    A Python 3.12 service runs pure-Python checksums, JSON canonicalization, and regex transforms on 50,000 payloads/min on a 16-vCPU, 8 GB RAM host. Wrapping it in `ThreadPoolExecutor(16)` dropped throughput from 1,200/s (1 thread) to 740/s (16 threads) with 35% `sys` CPU. Achieve near-linear 16-core scaling without pickle bottlenecks.

    Architecture

    CAP & PACELC Consistency-Latency Trade-Offs

    A global e-commerce service runs on a 3-region Raft cluster (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-south-1; RTTs: US-EU 75 ms, EU-IN 130 ms, US-IN 195 ms) with 60,000 RPS catalog reads (95%) and 3,000 RPS ledger writes (5%). Default PC/EC linearizable reads and writes push ap-south-1 checkout p99 past 390 ms and catalog reads past 150 ms (SLA < 120 ms). Redesign using PACELC.

  • 12
    Architecture

    Preventing Cassandra Tombstone Accumulation

    A Cassandra/ScyllaDB job scheduler ingests 200M tasks/day (~2,315/s avg, 10k/s peak, TTL=86400s + explicit DELETEs) into `PRIMARY KEY (queue_name, task_id)`. Polling `SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE queue_name = 'default' LIMIT 50` hits `TombstoneOverwhelmingException` (>100,000 tombstones) and 4.2 s p99 latency within 12 hours. Redesign the data model and compaction.
